Nigeria has confirmed one imported case of #Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), becoming the fifth country to detect the virus since an outbreak of the disease was declared in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) on 15 May 2026.

As per the Federal Ministry of Health, Nigeria (@Fmohnigeria):
▶️ The patient is a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda.
▶️ Her symptoms began on 7 October, four days after she arrived in Nigeria, and she sought care at a private health facility in Abuja on 11 October.
▶️ A laboratory test confirmed Bundibugyo virus on 20 October.
▶️ She is currently in isolation and receiving medical care.
▶️ Investigations are ongoing to establish the likely source of her infection and reconstruct her full travel and exposure history.

The ministry, so far, reports that 44 contacts have been identified and are being monitored. Contact tracing is also underway.

Rapid identification of cases, timely follow-up of contacts and effective infection prevention and control are critical to contain the spread of the virus.

WHO and partners are working with health authorities to strengthen efforts to stop the virus from spreading. 
WHO urges all countries in the region to sustain a high level of readiness as the outbreak in the DRC continues to evolve.
WHO advises against any restriction of travel to, or trade with, affected countries, and continues to closely monitor and, where necessary, verify travel and trade measures in relation to this event.
WHO regularly reviews the latest information to update its assessment of the risks posed by the outbreak.
Read the full press release: https://t.co/kM4nlqOGXe

DeepSeek just published the price of a token, and it should make you angry.

From their own DeepInfer docs: 1 cluster serves 155 trillion tokens a day, at $38 of revenue per GPU-hour, and thats at off-peak prices. Their API is $0.30 per million input tokens and $1.20 per million output at peak.

Yuchen Jin did the math: even if they rented B300s at $7 an hour, thats about 82% gross margin. Other estimates go higher.

So cheap AI is not charity and it is not "dumping". At these prices serving a frontier-class model is a very profitable business, if your inference stack is good enough.

Now remember every time a US lab told you that intelligence is expensive. That $200 a month is a fair price. That limits exist because compute is scarce.

Part of that is true. Part of it is a business model built on you not knowing what a token actually costs.

DeepSeek just showed everyone the numbers and gave away the engine. Every inference company can now compete on price with the same software. Thats how AI gets cheap for everyone.

SCOOP: Reuters Warns China’s Rare Earth Export Controls Could Return November 10 Despite Trade Truce Extension $MP $USAR $UUUU $UAMY $AREC 

As we know, the U.S. x China trade truce has officially been extended to January 10, 2027. 

However, according to Reuters, China’s expanded rare earth export controls are still scheduled to take effect on November 10, 2026, two months before the broader trade truce expires.

What’s crazy is… no one is talking about this. Not a soul. Except… cek.

Now here’s where the November 10 deadline becomes interesting:

Reuters specifically argues that these expanded rare earth restrictions were NOT included in the new $30 billion-for-$30 billion tariff reduction framework, and that September’s summit did not extend their implementation deadline.

China’s original suspension notice, Announcement No. 70, still explicitly lists November 10, 2026.

However, China’s September 28 statement extended the broader Kuala Lumpur arrangement to January 10, 2027, including an arrangement involving certain non-tariff measures.

That creates an important distinction: being excluded from the new tariff framework does not necessarily mean the rare earth controls were excluded from the broader truce extension.

As of October 20, I have not found an updated Chinese implementing notice explicitly moving the rare earth suspension deadline to January 10. If anyone can, please let me know.

If Reuters’ interpretation is correct, some of China’s most expansive rare earth restrictions could return in just three weeks, potentially affecting global semiconductor, AI, advanced manufacturing, and defense supply chains.

I’m particularly interested in hearing from anyone knowledgeable about Chinese trade regulations who has found a definitive government document resolving this discrepancy.

November 10 or January 10? The distinction matters.

Here’s what makes these restrictions particularly significant:

• 0.1% Threshold: Certain foreign-manufactured products containing Chinese-origin rare earth materials representing just 0.1% or more of the controlled item’s value could require Chinese export authorization.

• Global Reach: These restrictions could apply to qualifying products manufactured in the U.S., Europe, Japan, or elsewhere, even if the finished product never entered China.

• Technology Restrictions: The controls also target certain foreign-produced rare earth materials manufactured using Chinese-origin mining, separation, refining, magnet-making, or recycling technologies.

• Military Applications: Export licenses involving foreign military end users or military purposes would generally be denied under the original rules.

Source: Thomson Reuters Tax & Accounting

This chart shows the key risk to the AI trade, and it's missing from the latest revenue announcements.

The AI boom is fundamentally driven by a top 1% of companies that drive 80% of spend. Within that top 1%, 80% are venture-backed.

That's all fine if the AI trade works out, and if, as some prominent investors say, everyone wins.

But if it doesn't work out, then we have a cascading effect of large customers simultaneously pulling back their AI spend.
